utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Were you acquainted with the directives 7 and 7/1 issued by the Main Staff and the supreme commander and the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, when did the forward command post of Pribicevac, when was it technically capacitated and ready for work?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The forward command post of the Drina Corps in the village of Pribicevac in the technical sense, technically speaking, as far as communications, it being a communications centre, was ready for work in the afternoon hours of the 5th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: You told us about the establishment of communications with the units that were to participate, that is to say, participating in the combat operations and the establishment of communications with the superior command. Now, was this everything that you, as a professional man, did or are there any additional matters with respect to the general functioning of that centre that you had to see to?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to explain how I organised communications themselves?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, quite so.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The communication towards the superior command, that is to say, with the command of the Drina Corps in Vlasenica, that communication line, I organised by means of, one, a single channel via a radio relay device. And I did so by the fact that at the forward command post of Pribicevac, we brought a telephone switchboard and extension from the command facility of Crna Rijeka, and those same extensions we had in the command, that is to say, at the communications centre of the Drina Corps in Vlasenica. And so by dialing these mutually, we were able to ensure a direct communication. By using that same communication, via it, we were able to send out information, written information which was encrypted, protected. At the communications centre, I also had a device for the protection of oral information. And this oral protection, the protection of oral information, was possible towards the main command of the army of Republika Srpska. We were able to do that along that line. The communication towards the subordinate units I organised in a radio network of command with a protected device, and that was my sole communication towards the subordinate units which were participating in the Krivaja 95 operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: When you spoke about the sending out and reception of written messages, that is what we generally know as a teletype machine; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's right. It was a coded teletype communication, with the use of teletype and encryption devices.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: All that, then, was ready on the 5th of July; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the afternoon of the 5th of July, by the afternoon of the 5th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And you were there at the forward command post, you yourself?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Were you acquainted at the time with the plan, or rather, the -- yes, the plan of operation Krivaja 95?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the forward command post, after the arrival of the command to the forward command post, I was informed of the plan for Krivaja 95, in summary.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the plan was, Krivaja 95? What was it?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, in the military sense, we were to encircle the enclave of Srebrenica by deployment of our units and taking up the dominant features, assuming control of the dominant features in the vicinity of the demarcation line, delineation line, between our own forces and the forces of the 28th Division, and that line was in the vicinity of certain points which were controlled by UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: You mentioned dominant features. For the functioning and establishment of your communications, was that important?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was essential for me to have that knowledge and information because, with the subordinate units taking part in the Krivaja 95 operation, I had only one type of communication: radio link. And in view of the mountainous terrain around which the movements had to move, it was very important for me to know the assignment and their axis of attack so as to be able to have feedback information, that is to say, whether communications would always be top quality and continuous. So when I say this, I'm referring to it in the technical sense, technically speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So you learnt at the time which those elevation points were or the features that were the object of the activities of the units taking part in the attack?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Were those features Kak, Alibegovac, and Zivkovo Brdo?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Among the command staff, or rather, senior officers of the Drina Corps, who was present at the Pribicevac forward command post?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that at the Drina Corps forward command post in the region of the village of Pribicevac, the Chief of Staff, the then Chief of Staff of the Drina Corps, was present, that is, General Krstic, as the commander of the forward command post. There was Colonel Vicic, from the operations department of the Drina Corps, Lieutenant Colonel Svetozar Kosoric from the intelligence department, there was myself, and probably one of the non-commissioned officers from the staff command of the Drina Corps to service the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Was that the first time for you to go to the Pribicevac forward command post?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In that region and the area around it, I had been on several occasions, ever since the spring of 1993, when units of UNPROFOR entered the town of Srebrenica itself, and in the meantime I had been there on a number of occasions. And immediately prior to the operation Krivaja 95, I was in the region of the forward command post at the village of Pribicevac sometime at the beginning of June 1995, when units of the Drina Corps placed under their control the asphalt road going from Zeleni Jadar to Jasenova, Jelindol, Podravanje. Because this road, for the implementation of peace in the area, could not have been used until then; it was not possible to use it. Rather, our forces were not able to use it, even though it belonged to our territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Was the command staff at Pribicevac the same at the beginning of June, when you went there then?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that at the beginning of June the commander of this assignment was General Zivanovic, the commander of the Drina Corps, and I don't know who else, or rather, I don't remember who else among the senior officers of the Drina Corps was present. Probably one of the operations people, but I do not remember that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Witness DB, do you remember how the combat operations developed during those few days following the 6th of July?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recollect, the combat operations that were part of the Krivaja 95 operation started in the early morning of the 6th of July. The Drina Corps grouped the bulk of its forces along the axis Zeleni Jadar-Zivkovo Brdo, and I think the auxiliary forces had the task of breaking out from the broader region of Podravanje to the features of Kak and Alibegovac. During the first several days, or rather the first two days, combat contact was established with the enemy and surveillance was carried out by force, but there were no significant movement of the forces of either side, ours or the enemy forces. I think that it was on the third day, counting from the beginning of the operation, that our units along the main axis of attack managed to gain control of a feature called Zivkovo Brdo that was part of the defence system of the 28th Division. Along that axis the forces of the 28th Division put up strong resistance. I think that this feature was captured in the afternoon of that day. From the direction of Podravanje, according to my recollection, there was no significant resistance by the forces of the 28th Division, so that our units along that axis made advances without encountering any major difficulties. utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So we're talking about the period from the 6th until -- now we're talking about the 9th of July and the afternoon of the 9th. During those days, was General Krstic at the forward command post at Pribicevac?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what he was doing at the command post at Pribicevac during those days?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Krstic, throughout this time, was in command of the operation Krivaja 95.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: My question was with reference to the period from the 6th to the 9th, so when you say "all the time," do you mean that three-day period? Because we'll be going on to the period after the 9th later on.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I'm referring to this period that he was in command of his units and the operation Krivaja 95 during that period. He was in command of his units.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that using radio transmitters, he conveyed --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Objection. I'm going to object to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm going to object to my friend telling the witness what it means. I think the question should not be leading. It should perhaps be more open-ended. So my objection is, and I object to the reference to "Does that mean ..." because it is Mr. Petrusic who is testifying and not the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President, I just wanted to clarify the time that the witness was referring to, the time period, whether he meant the period from the 6th to the 9th of July.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Witness DB, in that period from the 6th until the 9th of July, do you have any knowledge as to how General Krstic would forward his orders to the brigade commanders?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that time period, General Krstic forwarded his orders to the brigade commanders within the command radio network which I described at the beginning of my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: At the forward command post, did you have reports from those communication lines on the situation on the front, or rather, along the lines of attack?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. General Krstic, by means of those communication lines, issued commands to his subordinate commanders and they reported to him using those same communication lines regarding the achievement of the tasks assigned to them and the situation on the front lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: By means of those communication lines, were you informed about the peace forces that were stationed there?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that one of the subordinate commanders, directly subordinate commanders, reported to General Krstic that at one of the UNPROFOR posts or checkpoints, an accident had occurred and that in a conflict or during a war conflict, a soldier had been killed. And we had that, the information that this soldier had been killed by members of the 28th Division and that the UNPROFOR soldiers at that post, finding themselves in an unfavorable situation for them at that time, and fearing the possibility of further adverse consequences, they pulled out to our side. What I mean is they crossed into territory that was under our control. I remember this because General Krstic ordered me personally at the time to go in the direction of Zeleni Jadar to find that group of UNPROFOR members and to escort them to safe territory in the region of the village of Pribicevac. That is what I did. I came across them in the vicinity of Zeleni Jadar as they were about to move in the direction of Pribicevac, and I escorted them to the region of the village of Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: When you said you escorted them, did they have their side weapons and equipment with them? I'm referring to APCs.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think there were three or four personnel carriers. They were marching alongside the APCs in a column, in a combat formation together with all the equipment and weapons they had, and I led them to safe territory in the region of the village of Pribicevac. And I am quite certain that, in that region, nothing could have -- nothing unforeseen could have happened to them. What is more, a number of our soldiers who happened to be there spoke and greeted them in a very friendly manner and they spoke in English. I think that someone offered them water. After that, I returned to the forward command post, that is the communications centre there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Witness DB, you are an officer and you are familiar with the concept and notion of taking captives. Can you describe this situation as taking members of UNPROFOR captive or capturing members of UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that situation has absolutely nothing in common with that term. Our behaviour towards them in the situation that I have just described was as between colleagues, between military men and officers, and I am quite sure I am not mistaken if I also add that it was, to a degree, a friendly attitude. I am saying this with reference to what I personally saw and the situation in which I participated.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you know where they went on from there, that is the UNPROFOR troops, that is, where they went from the region of the village of Pribicevac?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This group of three or four APCs, as far as I can recollect, stayed there for a while, and then I learned from someone that after they had established contact with their own command, they headed towards Bratunac, crossing through our territory, that is, territory controlled by our forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So you are linking this event to the 9th of July.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the day when they had one fatality, one killed soldier. And reconstructing the whole period, I assume that it could have been the 9th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: At the forward command post at Pribicevac, in addition to the officers you have mentioned, were there other officers of the Main Staff or the Drina Corps in the period from the 9th of July onwards?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the 9th of July until the completion of the operation, that is, until Srebrenica fell in military terms, I remember that at the forward command post, the commanders of the Main Staff did come, that is General Ratko Mladic, and the commander of the Drina Corps, General Zivanovic. I think they came on two or three consecutive days, and I also remember that one day, but I think this was only for a couple of hours, at the Pribicevac forward command post that General Gvero also came.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what General Mladic and General Zivanovic did during their visit to the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Zivanovic was accompanying or escorting General Mladic, or rather, they were always together. When they arrived at the forward command post, General Mladic would briefly inquire into the situation on the front in global terms, in general terms and, according to my recollection, on that occasion and on the occasion of several other operations, it was his custom personally using the radio link to confer with commanders of the directly subordinate units participating in the operation, telling -- to tell them, to congratulate them or to give them additional orders. I remember this because that was the customary behaviour of General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: On the 10th of July, was General Mladic at the forward command post at Pribicevac?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: On that day, did he get in touch with the subordinate units, the units actually carrying out combat operations?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to hear that?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Could you please explain to us, in addition to what you have already said about the operation of the communications system at the Pribicevac forward command post, tell us how it was possible for you to hear his messages that were transmitted through that communication system.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he came to the forward command post, and after being briefed about the situation, General Mladic would go to the observation post on the Kula feature, from where there is a very good view of the whole valley of Zeleni Jadar and Srebrenica, in fact, and all the surrounding features and the terrain in general. As a rule, together with him, General Zivanovic and General Krstic would go to the observation post. In order to be able to directly transmit orders from the observation post, I would order a soldier to carry a mobile transmitter to the observation post and to accompany them there with this equipment. The other transmitter would remain with me at the communications centre of the forward command post. So that we were all in one and the same network at the time, same radio network, both the observation post, where General Mladic was, and myself at the communications centre, and all the commanders of the directly subordinate units directly participating in the operation. In this way, I was able to hear the conversations that were being transmitted within that radio network.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: On that day, the 10th of July, did you hear conversations or orders issued by General Mladic to subordinate units?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Can you remember one of those orders or conversations?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember an incident that occurred very early in the morning, before dawn, in a counterattack by the forces of the 28th Division. Our forces were pushed back from Zivkovo Brdo and there were several killed soldiers on our side belonging to units whose task it had been to take up defensive positions on the lines they had reached. That battle went on until 7.00 or 8.00 in the morning of the 10th of July. At the time, we were taken aback by this new development, and I remember there was hasty regrouping of forces in preparation for an attack, for another counterattack to gain control of Zivkovo Brdo again. At that point in time, or about that time, I think it was about 9.00 or 10.00 in the morning, General Mladic appeared at the forward command post, together with General Zivanovic, and when he learnt about this development that had occurred that morning, he personally spoke to the then Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic, commander of the Zvornik Brigade, whose unit was attacking along that axis. And I remember that Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic said then that they would regain the feature, regain control of the feature, by 11.00 that day. I thought this was a brilliant military response at the time. And when he really did manage to recapture it sometime before midday, this made me remember the whole incident. After that event, General Mladic communicated over the radio with a number of commanders who were participating in the operation, and as far as I can recollect, as the overall combat situation at that moment appeared to be extremely favourable for our forces, because the dominant features had been captured, those immediately next to Srebrenica and some further away, I remember that General Mladic, in his communication with some of the commanders, ordered that the attack should resolutely be continued towards Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I must say, I have to interrupt the witness and his testimony, but my colleague tells me that General Krstic needs to be excused for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I was expecting that, and I gave you this authority. Thank you. So we'll adjourn for 15 minutes, till a quarter to one. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. Petrusic, we have been informed that General Krstic is not feeling in good shape. If he wants to waive his right to attend the trial, he is authorised to do so. If he can stay, he can stay with us until 1.30 and then we can adjourn for half an hour for the lunch period and resume until quarter to three. If he prefers not to be in the courtroom, you can ask him. I know the nurse is being fetched.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll all remain as we are until the next break. So General Krstic will attend up until the break and, depending how he feels after that, we shall be able to decide, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Witness DB, you have Exhibit 829 before you and I should like to ask the usher to place it on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Witness DB, you said that you had information that the dominant features that were to be taken control of by orders for active combat operations was Kak, Alibegovac, and Zivkovo Brdo; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: On the map in front of you, can you find those features for us, please, although we used another map previously, but could you point them out to us, please, on that map?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Would you point them out? Let's take Kak first.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kak is here. Alibegovac next, Alibegovac is here; and Zivkovo Brdo is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Witness DB, now between the Kak and Alibegovac features, will you draw a line with your felt tip marker. I think you have a marker in front of you, a red one. Will you draw a line between those two points, please. Join the two features up.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Next, from Alibegovac towards Zivkovo Brdo. Will you do the same and draw a line between those two points.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Witness DB, are you acquainted with the Bojna feature?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Can you find it for us on the map, please?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Would you draw a circle around the feature Bojna.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: According to your knowledge, sir -- just one moment, please. I withdraw that question upon the suggestion of my colleague, Mr. Visnjic. Now, along these lines, the lines that you have linked up, Kak, Alibegovac, and Zivkovo Brdo, those areas that you have linked up, will you please put your initials "DB" for us.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: That will be difficult to decipher as being DB because you have written them in Cyrillic but, for the purposes of the record, let us note that the witness has written in his initials DB in the Cyrillic script. Can you do the same for the Bojna feature, please; also place your Cyrillic initials there.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Thank you. After gaining these lines and taking control of those features, the ones that we mentioned, did General Mladic, through radio communication, issue orders to his subordinate commanders?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that, after our units broke through to these features and assumed control, he congratulated the commanders on having done so through radio link, radio communication and, at the same time, he hurried them up so to speak, to continue and -- in a further attack. Whether he dictated the axis of attack to the units on that occasion or not, I can't remember at this point. But at any rate, each unit had to receive an axis of attack. But I do remember him speeding up the commanders, urging them on. And sometime on the 10th, in the afternoon, perhaps even at about 7.00 or 8.00 p.m., when Colonel Andric, the then Colonel Andric, the commander of the 1st Birac Brigade, informed him that after his order he was still engaged in this assignment and that he had still to take control of the Vagan feature. I remember that very well. I remember it well when, according to his assessment, he energetically ordered him to bypass that particular feature and to continue his attack further so that his men would not become too exhausted by taking control of that particular feature, because I felt at the time that General Mladic thought that there were no forces at that feature belonging to the 28th Division.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Can you find that feature on the map, please, because we have mentioned it for the first time, Vagan.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's this feature here. It's this feature here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Please put your initials in Cyrillic, please, DB. So those were the activities that you described and which, to the best of your recollection, took place on the 10th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Let us now stay with the 10th of July for a moment. General Zivanovic and General Krstic, were they in command then and did they issue orders to the units at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that General Zivanovic did not appear in the command network, and I also think -- I also do not think that General Krstic appeared either. That is how I remember that period and that particular day.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Witness DB, may we move on to the 11th of July now, 1995. You were at the forward command post, were you not?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I continued to be at the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Was the composition of the superior officers the same with respect to the previous day?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened, what was taking place at the command post that day and what the commanding officers' activities were, depending on developments on the front?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That particular day, the attack by our units was continued on the basis of the order given the previous day. I think that at one point General Mladic, together with Generals Zivanovic and Krstic, transferred to an observation post in the region of the Kvarac feature. Whether that was immediately before the NATO airstrikes -- I think it was, yes, which would make it sometime around midday. And I know that it is from that observation post at Kvarac that communication continued and commanding of the operation continued from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Would you show us that area, please, on the map, the Kvarac feature. Where is it? For purposes of the record, we have your initials in Cyrillic there again. The aviation, that is to say, the NATO airstrikes, took place?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That day, there were NATO airstrikes attacking our forces located -- that is to say, in combat with the forces of the 28th Division, and I think that those strikes, that bombing, took place in the Bojna region, and they attacked the forces of the 1st Zvornik Infantry Brigade. I think that there was machine-gun fire around the broader region of Pribicevac sometime around 1.00 p.m. or 2.00 p.m., after midday.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: You said that, according to your recollections, Mladic, Zivanovic and Krstic went to the Kvarac area. Did they return to the Pribicevac forward command post?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be quite sure now whether they returned or not during the afternoon. I think they did come back from the Kvarac area to Pribicevac. I think they returned sometime in the afternoon, that is to say, after the NATO airstrikes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And finally, did you -- via your communications centre and the subordinate units, did information reach you that either parts of the units or their commanders had entered the town?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At the communications centre, following developments via our radio devices, we learnt that all the defences of the 28th Division of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina had ceased and that parts of our own units had entered the town itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: These three commanding officers, Mladic, Zivanovic and Krstic, the generals, did they go into town?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Sometime during the afternoon, at about 1700 or 1800 hours or thereabouts, with their heavy vehicles, terrain vehicles, they went off towards the town itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So after their departure, who stayed on at the Pribicevac forward command post?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: After their departure from the forward command post, of the officers at that forward command post, only I myself remained and probably some of the subordinate officers from the staff command.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: You said earlier on that, in the course of those days and in the establishment of the former command post, that Colonel Vicic and Colonel or Lieutenant Colonel Kosoric arrived there. Now on that day, the 11th of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. July, were they at the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were at the forward command post on that day too, but following an assignment, they left the region. Whether before the group of generals or immediately after the generals, I can't say. I can't remember. But what I do know is that I was the sole remaining officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: The officers that we mentioned and -- that is to say, Generals Mladic, Zivanovic, and Krstic, did they return to the forward command post of Pribicevac at all?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was at the command post that day, the forward command post, they did not return.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And how long did you stay at the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stayed at the forward command post until 1900 hours or thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And did you leave the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took stock of the situation and the new developments, and as I was able to control the lines and developments via radio relay, I thought that the communications centre was no longer needed at Pribicevac, that there was no need for it anymore and so I packed it up. When I say "packed up," that is a term we use. And at around 1900 hours or a little after that, a little later, I went off towards the command of the Bratunac Brigade, the Bratunac Brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: You say "packed up the communications centre"; can you explain what that actually implies, the term to "pack up," what does that imply?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, according to our regulations, we have that term to install and to pack up the communications centre, both to install and establish means to establish all the communications that have been planned; and to pack up the communications centre quite simply means what it says, to discontinue those communications and to place the devices and vehicles -- to put them on the march, and to prepare to establish communication centres elsewhere where they are needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So does that mean that, up until the 11th of July, as you say, at around 1900 hours, that is to say, on the 11th of July when you left Pribicevac, the communications centre at that particular command post no longer existed? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: At that forward command post, that particular feature, was there some other form of communication, telephone communication, apart from the one you yourself helped establish?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At that feature, what remained was part of the units. I think it was the independent Skelani Battalion, part of the battalion stayed on, and they had their own internal communication. That is to say, between the trenches or the defence lines in the defence system that had previously been established before the Krivaja 95 operation was launched.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: With that type of communication that you say existed within the defence lines of the Skelani Battalion, were they able to communicate in the way in which had previously been done by the communications centre that you, yourself, established on the 5th of July; was that possible?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: That is to say, there were no communications with the -- no communications were possible with what was left of the Skelani Battalion with the Corps Command, for example?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because there were no technical facilities for doing so after the communications centre that I had established and installed had been packed up.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: You said, sir, that you left for the command of the -- the headquarters of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Which route did you take?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took the route going from Pribicevac to Bojna, to Srebrenica, Potocari, Zuti Most, Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: When you passed through Srebrenica, you encountered the army there.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I passed through that town for the first time on that occasion. I noticed some soldiers belonging to the army of Republika Srpska in the town itself along the streets, but not more than ten of them, about ten.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And in the town itself -- I suppose you went down the main street -- did you happen to notice the traces of fighting, shelling?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what Srebrenica looked like before that. I noticed on the facades of the houses that there were holes from infantry weapons. There were no more visible traces of any major combat activities compared to some other places that I had passed through during the war. I remember that the town itself looked fairly dirty and in disarray, and it is situated in a valley, in a depression, so the impression was not a nice one. But there weren't any major traces of combat activity in the town itself, I can't say that in the sense of any major destruction or anything of that kind. I didn't notice anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Did you notice any civilians or any members of the 28th Division, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the road from Srebrenica to Potocari, at several points along the road, along that route, I noticed towards Potocari the -- I noticed two or three civilians moving that way. They were elderly persons, for the most part, and they were carrying some bags and things like that with them. But there weren't too many of them. I did notice several of them moving towards Potocari along the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Did you pass through Potocari?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Was -- what about the members of UNPROFOR; did they prohibit passage through Potocari at all?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not encounter any checkpoints or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And in Potocari itself, did you see any civilians yourself there?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in Potocari itself, in the place itself, both on the left and right-hand side of the road, I did see a large number of civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: I think we'll agree that they were Muslims, were they not?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were Muslims. And for me, that was a new and surprising image in the war, a large number of civilians. And it was already getting dark, dusk was falling, but I didn't stop my vehicle. I moved slowly onwards to make it safe for the civilians. So I moved as slowly as I could, moving in the presence of such a large number of civilians. I took care to move slowly. And I noticed that these civilians seemed to be mixed up with the UNPROFOR soldiers. At several points amongst the civilians I noticed members of UNPROFOR. I also noticed a number of soldiers belonging to the army of Republika Srpska and they were all there together mixed up, and they were discussing something. The soldiers had their rifles on their shoulders, not in the combat position. Quite simply, there seemed to be some curiosity going on, some inquisitiveness, and they were communicating about something of this large number of civilians all together, members of UNPROFOR together with the civilians and some Republika Srpska soldiers. But the communication that was going on amongst all these people, as far as I was able to notice, was not a war situation. I thought that perhaps those soldiers, the army of Republika Srpska soldiers were perhaps from the town itself, from the town of Srebrenica who had been holding positions up until then around the enclave or that they were some other soldiers who happened to know some of the civilians. That was the impression I gained. I was surprised to see this -- to see that only a few hours before that, there had been fighting and war going on whereas at that particular moment, everybody was talking to everybody else in a sort of inquisitive way.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Now, this image that you gained, this impression that you gained as you were passing the presence of the soldiers from Republika Srpska and so on, their presence, it did not give the impression that there was any hostility going on, is that right, or any mistreatment of those civilians or any -- or that they were behaving towards the civilians in a way that would not be customary and which would represent a violation of the laws and customs of --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This is a leading question. I object to the form of the question. I think the witness can be asked his impression, but again, my learned friend is leading the witness by providing the answer to him in his question, and I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: This time, Mr. Petrusic, I agree. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree too, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Let's put it again. Was there any hostility in the impression that you had of this conduct on the part of the army of Republika Srpska towards the civilians?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: As you passed through Potocari, following on from that, you went along the road towards Bratunac; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Let me go back for a moment. How many Serb soldiers were there in this crowd of refugees and UNPROFOR soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot now tell you with certainty, but I am quite sure that what I saw were small groups of soldiers, two or three, or individuals, talking to certain groups. So all in all, as I was passing, I didn't see more than 10 to 20 Serb soldiers along the road that I passed along, to my left and right, as far as I was able to see, because it was already getting dark by then.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So you were heading towards Bratunac. Along that road from Potocari to Bratunac, did you see groups of Serb soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. On the road from Potocari to Zuti Most, or Yellow Bridge, I think I did not come across anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So you reached Bratunac, the headquarters of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I arrived in Bratunac around 2130 hours, or 2100 hours. Anyway, it was already quite dark, so my estimate is that it could have been that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Who did you find, or where were any -- were your soldiers, your soldiers who were with you at the communications centre?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: When leaving the communications centre and the forward command post, as a rule, together with General Krstic and a mobile receiver, a signalsman would go with him. Whether this always happened, I cannot say, but that would be the rule, so that General Krstic could communicate, while being on the move, with units taking part in an operation from some other location, as far as the technical possibilities allowed, that is, within the range of those devices. The other soldiers from the communications centre went with me, and a vehicle, a large vehicle with -- the communication system vehicle, where we always had a mobile centre assembled, passed through Srebrenica with me, Potocari, and we arrived at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters sometime after 2100 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Would it be suitable for you now to break?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrusic. We'll resume at 2.00. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.32 p.m. 24 25

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I hope General Krstic is feeling better.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. We'll continue in General Krstic's presence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you. Please resume.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Witness DB, before we pick up where we left off, that is your arrival at Bratunac, my question is: Are you aware that, according to establishment, there was in the army of Republika Srpska a 10th Sabotage Detachment?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you know under whose command, direct command was that unit?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 10th Sabotage Detachment was a unit directly subordinated to the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: The Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: In the period from the 5th of July when you set up the communications centre at Pribicevac until the 11th of July in the afternoon or early evening when this centre was packed up or dismantled, was the unit of the 10th Sabotage Detachment linked by communications to your system?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: In that time period, therefore, could anyone from the forward command post at Pribicevac, through the system of communication lines that was operative there, establish contact with them?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through the system of communications that I organised for the operation Krivaja 95, it was not possible to command that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge about their presence, the presence of the 10th Sabotage Detachment in the area of combat operations at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that they arrived in the area only a day or two before Srebrenica fell militarily, which means a day or two prior to the 11th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So you do know that they were there?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I personally saw their signalsman so we exchanged a couple of words related to communications because I was wondering whether they would have any assignment or not. However, they were not covered by our communications system so I don't know exactly who gave them assignments. But in any event, their signalsman told me that they would not enter our communication system, that is the communication system used to command that operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: According to your knowledge, they were not in the communication system in the period from the 5th to the 11th?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were not in the system at all in that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: When you arrived in Bratunac and you said it was 9.00 in the evening or half past 9.00, who did you find there?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the compound of the Bratunac Brigade headquarters, I remember seeing a vehicle which had brought General Krstic there, because I found there my soldier, a signalsman who was carrying with him this mobile device for the needs of General Krstic that afternoon of the 11th. So I asked him whether there were any news, whether I had been called by anyone because, according to my own assessment, I left the forward command post in the evening and I asked whether General Krstic had arrived there. He told me that General Krstic had arrived and that he had come with him along a different route, that they had not passed through Potocari, that he had tried to reach me over the mobile device to convey to me a couple of messages but I had already left the forward command post. I then felt it necessary for me to report to General Krstic, to inform him that I had left, and that I had packed up the communications centre at the forward command post and that that communications centre no longer existed at Pribicevac. I think that my signalsman or someone else told me that there would be a meeting shortly in the Bratunac Brigade headquarters and that General Krstic would be there, so I headed in that direction to report to him and to tell him, let him know that I was in the brigade headquarters too now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: You mean in the command of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Did your signalsman tell you what route General Krstic had taken upon leaving Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't come through Potocari and Zuti Most along that route. In fact, he found it strange that when I told him that I had passed through that area of Potocari. I think he told me that they took another route via Pribicevac and Sase because in passing, he mentioned that already around 2000 hours, just before dark, they had caught up with a couple of soldiers probably from the Bratunac Brigade who had, until then, held defensive positions in the area, that they were pushing in front of them a small herd of sheep, probably from a Muslim village. And I remember this because he told me how he had to get into a jeep in the back seat where it was crowded because -- it was cramped, because General Krstic was furious with these two soldiers, that he apparently criticised them very hard and, in fact, he ordered the signalsman of mine that should any one of them utter a word, that he should hit him with his rifle butt, and he personally drove those two soldiers in his vehicle to the military prison at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: As far as I am able to understand, those two soldiers that you assume were from the Bratunac Brigade had in fact stolen that livestock?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These were some petty thieves. When the front line was moved, they probably took advantage of the opportunity to pick up that herd for their own needs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Among the officers, who did you find in the Bratunac Brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I entered the hall where the meeting was held. Just then it hadn't started yet, and I think it started around 2200 hours. I know that present at the meeting were General Mladic, General Zivanovic, General Krstic, I think. Logically, all the commanders of the directly subordinated units that had taken part in Krivaja 95 were also present, and also some other officers, but I do not recollect now who.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you have any recollection as to the contents of the meeting that you are referring to that was held on the 11th in the evening?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seemed to me that the meeting did not have a strictly military content that was precise and clear, as was customary, because there was a feeling of victory, a celebratory atmosphere, probably because of the outcome of the combat operations. And the meeting was chaired, or rather the main say was held by the commander of the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska, General Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And what was the topic of the meeting?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that General Mladic praised the units for their success; he underlined their successes in the operation. And I remember also that just then he conveyed his idea or gave orders that immediately all the units which had participated in the operation Krivaja 95 had to be transferred to new areas in order to prepare for the attack on Zepa. It seems to me that he said that a plan had to be done immediately and that General Krstic should prepare the plan and that, with all the units that had participated in Srebrenica, should immediately be transferred for the offensive operation against Zepa. General Mladic, while saying this, and as he noticed me sitting there in the hall, he ordered me that I should immediately, that same evening, immediately head for a new forward command post in the region of the village of Krivace [Realtime transcript read in error "Pribicevac"] to establish a communications centre there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think we have an error in the transcript. The witness said "in the region of the village of Krivace," and in the transcript we see "the village of Pribicevac."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So let us correct this through a question. Did you get an order Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. to set up a forward command post in the village of Krivace, near Zepa?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: That concept or order, as you put it, at the meeting, did anyone oppose that or did you all accept it as such?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember after this concept had been presented, or order, that the then Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic addressed General Mladic. He was the commander of the 1st Zvornik Infantry Brigade. And he pointed out that the situation in the broader region of Srebrenica was, in military terms, rather unclear, that forces of the army of Republika Srpska who were in pursuit of the enemy had not managed to establish combat contact with them anywhere and that again we had no information that the units which had held defensive positions earlier on in other parts of the enclave, that there were reports that soldiers of the 28th Division were endeavouring to break through. For this reason, Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic suggested that the situation should first be cleared up in the military sense around Srebrenica so that this should not provoke any fresh problems. However, I cannot now quote or even paraphrase the answer General Mladic gave, but in general terms it could be interpreted as the following: Regardless of that, all for Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Did you draw any conclusions from that, if it is possible at all to talk about conclusions?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, I was the youngest at the meeting, but the suggestion and the thoughts conveyed by Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic seemed to me to be quite logical and justified, because I had up to then already had appreciation for his military capabilities and the fact that he was capable of presenting his own views and positions to General Mladic, who in those days was considered to be an unquestionable military authority among soldiers and officers alike. I think that General Mladic had his own assessment on the basis of which he had made this idea and decision, he had taken this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Did you have any knowledge about the officer cadres, if I can call them that, that had gathered at that meeting? What was your opinion? Why was it that Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic addressed General Mladic; do you have any explanation for that?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was because our forces were in pursuit of the enemy from the south-east towards the north or north-west. And it was expected that the forces of the 28th Division would try to make a breakthrough towards the north or northwestern part of the enclave and their advances towards the territory of the 2nd Corps of the BH army through the area of responsibility of the Zvornik Brigade. And I think because he was the commander of that brigade, he thought that there was a danger for his own area of responsibility and that is why he made that suggestion. Secondly, Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic, in that particular situation, felt that it was logical for the situation to be cleared up militarily. At the time, he was the commander of a brigade which numbered between 5.000 and 6.000 men. And with his unit, he was a pillar of support for the Drina Corps in many battles even in other theatres of war outside that area. He was considered an authority among other commanders. And as I said, he had a say of his own and he didn't hesitate to convey his opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: When you were given the order orally on the 11th in the evening at that meeting to go and set up a communications centre at Krivace, was that sufficient for you to set up technically that future centre, or rather, the future forward command post?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. For me, that was quite sufficient. I knew the location of the new forward command post. I heard the order that all the units that had been at Srebrenica should march forward and prepare for an offensive operation on Zepa so that I know who the participants were. I knew where the forward command post would be, and that was quite sufficient for me. So I sat there for a very short while, waiting, whether perhaps in the course of these consultations, there might be some additional information or any change which would affect my organisation of communications. And when I saw that there were no additional information, that same evening, with the communication centre already packed, and with my soldiers, I went from Bratunac in the direction of the command of the Drina Corps in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: What route did you take for Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I arrived at Vlasenica from Bratunac via Krivace, Konjevic Polje, and Milici.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: On that road from Bratunac to Vlasenica, did you come across members of the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. I think it was only in the region of Krivace and Konjevic Polje along the road that there was some ambushes being prepared and I think that I saw members of the MUP, Ministry of Interior Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Are you sure that they -- that it was them or is that a supposition on your part?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was them because they had the characteristic uniform predominantly blue. Had it been the army, I should have known that in view of the units which took part in the operation Krivaja 95, and as I monitored the situation, I know that in that region, there would not have been any, so to speak, reserve units of the army there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: When did you arrive in Vlasenica at the command headquarters of the corps?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I arrived at the Corps Command at around 2400 hours or thereabouts on the 11th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: From there, did you carry on towards Krivace because you had an order to set up a command centre?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Moving towards Vlasenica, I had something wrong with my vehicle, something had gone wrong with the vehicle, and there was some knocking noise in the wheels. And when we reached Vlasenica, after the driver had looked at the vehicle and told me that a whole spare part had to be replaced and taken from another vehicle, he informed me of that. But that vehicle was very important because we had installed all the devices necessary for a mobile communications centre on it. I can't now remember whether, at the corps headquarters, I asked permission from anybody because, at that time, I don't think that there was anybody in the Drina Corps command headquarters who had the authority to give me permission to spend the night in Vlasenica or perhaps I assessed the situation myself and decided to spend the night there. But anyway, I stayed there that night in Vlasenica and didn't go on to Krivace to repair the car, the vehicle, and that's where we spent the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: In Vlasenica at the headquarters of the corps, is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you remember who you came across there of the officers in the Corps Command?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was late. Perhaps the duty operations officer was there but I don't remember who it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And the next day, on the 12th of July, in the morning, what were your activities then?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next day, early in the morning we worked fast to repair the vehicle and to prepare everything else necessary for our new assignment. They were technical preparations, all the material that we needed for the communications centre and I think that the new forward command post towards Krivace we started at sometime around midday, at around 12.00 noon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: From the 11th in the evening when you left the meeting in Bratunac, up to your departure for Krivace at about 12.00 the next day on July 12th, did you have any communication with General Krstic, or rather, anyone from the Corps Command?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think General Krstic stayed in Bratunac on the 11th, and I did not see him until my departure for Krivace.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Did you come across anybody in Krivace on the 12th of July, upon your arrival?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the immediate vicinity, that is to say some 50 to 100 metres away from the place, we set up the communications centre on the 12th of July. There was a unit there from the 65th Protection Motorised Regiment and they had a defence position there that they held from earlier on, and it was 285th Zepa Brigade, that is to say, they were close by. So I found them there, and some two or three kilometres away, there was the command of a battalion in the village of Plane, a battalion belonging to the 65th Motorised Protective Division, but I didn't go to them on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: As you mentioned the 65th Protection Regiment, do you know which unit held that resistance point, defence point?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I think it might have been a platoon. They had one or two combat vehicles perhaps, so it was perhaps a platoon of one of the companies from that battalion in Plane.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And the battalion in Plane, do you know anything about that? Was it an infantry battalion, or what?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was an infantry battalion, although in that particular region, whether before or afterwards, there were some armoured units as well, but I think that, at that time, it was an infantry battalion. At least, those were the kinds of weapons they had. That is what I would say. That is how it appeared to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: On the 12th of July, in the course of the day and the evening, while you were there at Krivace, did anybody appear of the command staff at that forward command post? Did anybody come?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. On that day, we had a lot of work to do to install the communications centre, to camouflage the devices and set up the defence. And I remember that, on that particular day, which was the 12th of July, the day that I arrived at the new command post in the village of Krivace, nobody from the command of the Drina Corps turned up. I didn't see anybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: That communications centre, had it been installed for use on the 12th of July? Was it ready to function, technically speaking?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Technically speaking, it could have been used. It was operative and operational and all the communications were ready to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: On the 13th of July, that is to say, the 13th of July, did any of the commanding officers come to the forward command post of Krivace at all?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 13th of July, I think somebody did appear at the forward command post, but conditionally speaking, it was a whole team from the Drina Corps in the Krivaja 95 operation, which means General Krstic, Colonel Vicic, and Lieutenant Colonel Kosoric. Now, whether that was before noon, in the afternoon, or in the evening, I really can't say. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So on that 13th of July, the communications centre was operational; it could function unimpeded and serve its purpose, the purpose for which it had been set up?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Sometimes we had some minor problems with the power supply, and we had a generator with us, but those problems were not so frequent. And I know that the -- they did not have any vital effect on command, so these problems did not affect command. There were no serious interruptions, so we could go ahead with those communications without any great problems. There were certain interruptions, but it was possible to command.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Before we end for the day, Witness DB, could you explain to us the functioning of the communications centre, that is to say, from Krivace towards the subordinate and superior commands.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It functioned on the basis of exactly the same principle and with all the same details as it did in the Krivaja 95 operation. The terrain was different, that was all. But otherwise, all the principles were the same as they were for the communications centre in the village of Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So from that communications centre, if I understand you correctly, there was no direct communication with the commands of the original units who were taking part in the operation towards Zepa; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO BOROVCANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Technically speaking, we did not have the possibility from the command posts [Realtime transcript read in error "forward command post"], both Pribicevac and Krivace, to receive -- to reach the commands of the original units directly in the locations where they were. But if that was indispensable, if we had to communicate with them, then we would do so through the mediation of the communications centre at the command headquarters of the Drina Corps in Vlasenica. So we would ring them up, and that communications centre had all the original matrix, commands and connections, and then the switchboard operator would connect us further on. So we didn't have direct communication, but technically we were able to connect via the communications centre in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we have an objection to make with respect to the transcript. On line 23, which is on the screen, page 86, it was the forward command post, and the witness said, "We had no possibility from both forward command posts, Pribicevac and Krivace." The forward command post [as interpreted], not just "the command post," as it says in the transcript. The forward command post [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: It stands corrected.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: It stands corrected now after the intervention. Yes, Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence would end there for today with respect to the examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Petrusic. We resume tomorrow at 9.20, and I believe it will be in Courtroom 3. [Interpretation] Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you. Tomorrow at 9.20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
